rationale:
Issue #1570 reports that the dart_style formatter incorrectly emits a trailing comma when splitting catch clause parameters, producing syntactically invalid Dart code. The minimized production patch changes exactly one call site in piece_factory.dart to pass `const ListStyle(commas: Commas.nonTrailing)` to DelimitedListBuilder when formatting catch clauses, eliminating the erroneous trailing comma. The trigger tests added in the fix commit are golden formatting fixtures (try.stmt and try_comment.stmt) that specify expected output for split catch clauses with and without stack traces, demonstrating both the defect (trailing comma before closing paren) and the correction. Strict runtime validation confirms both triggers fail deterministically on buggy revision f46aa311 and pass on fixed revision f5caa5c4, with full-suite runs showing no unrelated failures. The patch introduces no new API, refactoring, documentation, or feature changes—only the comma style parameter at the catch-clause formatting site. No active same-project root causes exist, so no duplication.

Strict validation confirms both triggers (try.stmt and try_comment.stmt) fail differentially on buggy f46aa311 and pass on fixed f5caa5c4 across 3 repetitions with deterministic fingerprints. The test patch contains only fixture additions that exercise the exact defect scenario described in the issue (split catch clauses), with no new production API or unrelated changes. No active same-project root causes exist to duplicate.
